title: My Daily Routine
description: Describe the main actions in a typical day in sequence.
objectives: Describe the main actions in a typical day in sequence.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to describe the main actions in a typical day in sequence. The central language is present simple first-person routine verbs. It belongs to the practical context of daily life. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A1, keep the message short and concrete. One clear sentence is enough before the other person responds. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the my daily routine exchange.
This my daily routine model adds a different detail or response.

blocks.english: What do you do every day?
blocks.explanation: Use this question or response to keep the my daily routine exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “I wake up at seven.” and “I have breakfast before work.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: present simple first-person routine verbs.
